title: Coral Reefs, Atolls and Marine Ecosystems

cards.h: Reefs are small in area but huge in life
cards.b: Coral reefs cover under 1 percent of the ocean floor but shelter about a quarter of marine species. They protect coasts and feed millions. They are under threat from warming seas. UPSC asks about reef types, Darwin's theory, bleaching and Indian reefs.

Corals are tiny animals called polyps. They build hard skeletons of calcium carbonate. Inside their tissue live algae called zooxanthellae, which give colour and food through photosynthesis.

Reef corals need clear, shallow, warm water: 20 to 30 degrees C, salinity of about 32 to 36 parts per thousand, depth under about 50 m, and sunlight. They do not grow near river mouths, where fresh and muddy water harms them.

Fringing reef: grows right against the shore, with a shallow, narrow lagoon or none. Common round Andaman islands. Barrier reef: separated from land by a wide, deep lagoon. The Great Barrier Reef is the largest. Atoll: a ring of coral enclosing a lagoon, with no central land. Lakshadweep and the Maldives are mostly atolls.

Charles Darwin (1842, The Structure and Distribution of Coral Reefs) proposed that a fringing reef grows around a volcanic island. As the island slowly sinks, the coral grows upward to stay near light. The reef becomes a barrier reef, then an atoll when the island vanishes.

Drilling at Eniwetok atoll in the 1950s found volcanic rock beneath over a kilometre of coral, supporting Darwin.

Daly's glacial control theory: sea level fell in the ice age, planing islands flat; rising seas then let coral grow upward. Murray's theory: reefs build on submarine platforms. Today most geologists accept a mix: subsidence plus sea-level change.

The Great Barrier Reef (about 2,300 km, Queensland, Australia) is the largest. The Belize Barrier Reef is the biggest in the Atlantic. Atolls are common in the Maldives, Lakshadweep, Marshall Islands and Tuvalu. Reefs lie mainly between 30 degrees N and S in the Indo-Pacific and the Caribbean.

When water gets too warm, corals expel their algae and turn white. They are not dead but starving. If the heat persists, they die. The Great Barrier Reef suffered mass bleaching in 1998, 2002, 2016, 2017, 2020 and 2022.

Other threats: ocean acidification (absorbing CO2 weakens skeletons), crown-of-thorns starfish, destructive fishing, and sediment runoff.

Mangroves grow in salty tidal mud and shelter fish nurseries. Seagrass meadows feed dugongs and turtles. Estuaries mix river and sea water and are among the most productive zones. Upwelling zones (Peru, Namibia, Somalia) are rich in plankton and fish. Deep-sea vents run on chemical energy rather than sunlight.

The photic zone, the top 200 m or so, holds most marine life because light reaches it. Phytoplankton there make about half of the oxygen we breathe.

Four main reef areas: Gulf of Mannar (Tamil Nadu), Gulf of Kachchh (Gujarat), Lakshadweep (atolls) and Andaman and Nicobar (fringing reefs). Gulf of Mannar was declared a biosphere reserve in 1989, the first marine one in South and Southeast Asia. Coral is also protected under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.

Likely questions: 'Explain the types of coral reef and the conditions for growth', 'Discuss Darwin's theory', 'Causes and effects of coral bleaching'.

  • List the conditions in five bullets.
  • Draw fringing, barrier and atoll in one line each.
  • End with conservation: marine protected areas, reducing emissions, coral restoration.
